//: DO NOT hand-edit. Generate this from the web app's appsettings so the storage connection strings have one source of truth: pwsh ./Sync-FunctionSettings.ps1 -Environment Test
//why-one-file: The QueueTrigger attributes resolve their queue names (%MediaProcessing:*QueueName%) and their storage connection (StagingStorageConnectionString) through the Functions HOST, before the worker's IConfiguration exists. A per-environment appsettings.*.json loaded by the worker could not supply them, which is why every setting lives here rather than being split across two mechanisms.
//in-azure: There are no settings files in Azure. Each of the two Function Apps carries its own Application Settings, and that is the per-environment mechanism. Sync-FunctionSettings.ps1 -ShowAzureCli prints the az command to push these same values up.
//not-azurite: The values below are placeholders. In practice Development points at the REAL storage accounts (musiccontainer-local / musicuploads-local), matching how the web app already treats Development - so running func start locally polls a real queue.

Values.//AzureWebJobsStorage: Functions runtime bookkeeping. Shares the standard account with the queues.
Values.//StagingStorageConnectionString: STANDARD general-purpose account: the queues and the upload staging container. Read/write. Premium accounts have no Queue service, which is the whole reason there are two accounts.
Values.//MediaStorageConnectionString: PREMIUM account holding song media. Read for the probe path, write for cover-art renditions ONLY - the web app is still the sole writer of every primary blob and of the database. Nothing here may touch a blob a SongMetadata row already points at.
Values.//MediaProcessing:MatchQueueName: Cover-art pairing queue. Referenced as %...% in the trigger, so the HOST resolves it - if it is missing the trigger cannot bind and the WHOLE Function App fails to start, not just this function.
Values.//MediaProcessing:PackageQueueName: Encrypted-HLS packaging queue. Same %...% binding constraint as the others - a missing value stops the WHOLE Function App from starting. A separate queue from the transcode rather than a second step inside it, because host.json pins batchSize:1 so one instance handles one message: two full FFmpeg passes under a single 10-minute Consumption ceiling would fail long songs at the second one having already succeeded at the first.
Values.//MediaProcessing:StreamingContainerName: Where encrypted HLS packages are written, on the PREMIUM account beside the media container. Private, like every other container - segment URLs carry a container read SAS the web app stamps on. It holds AES-128 ciphertext and a manifest whose key URI is a placeholder. NEVER write anything unencrypted here; its contents are handed to listeners.
Values.//CallbackBaseUrl: Where results are posted. Must match the environment the queues belong to.
Values.//MediaProcessingApiKey: Must equal the top-level MediaProcessingApiKey in the web app's appsettings for the same environment.
Values.//OpenAI:ApiKey: OPTIONAL, unlike everything above. Powers the vision OCR and pairing call behind cover-art matching. Leave blank or at the placeholder and the Function pairs on filenames alone - a worse answer, not a broken one, and uploads still work.
